context_summary: F58 adds 3 new level elements from B-09 (first batch): Spring (bounces Mel upward), Moving Platform (horizontal or vertical, configurable speed/range), and Spikes (instant damage on contact). Each becomes a new EntityType, a new React component with Rapier physics, and a new entry in the editor palette. These elements are essential for interesting campaign level design.

options_considered.description: Implement each element as an EntityType + React component + editor palette entry. Spring uses a sensor+impulse, Moving Platform uses a kinematic body with configurable props (direction, speed, range), Spikes use a sensor with damage callback.
pros: Each element is independent — can be implemented in parallel
Follows existing entity pattern (Coin, Heart, Checkpoint, Goal, Enemy)
Props system in EntityData already supports configuration (direction, speed, range)
LevelSceneConverter already handles unknown entity types via otherEntities
cons: Moving Platform needs kinematic body which is a new physics pattern for this codebase
Need to extend EntityType union in shared/types.ts

rationale: Standard entity pattern is the right approach. Each element follows the established Coin/Heart/Enemy pattern: EntityType + component + editor palette. The moving platform's kinematic body is a well-documented Rapier pattern. Props configuration keeps the editor simple (dropdowns for direction/speed). All 3 elements are independent and can be developed in parallel.
